Today is the start of the Lyrid meteor shower. Visible: 16-25 Apr, Peak: 22/23 Apr +MP:-04-22+, ZHR: 15-20, Radiant: Lyra. Bright fast meteors, some with trains. Associated with Comet Thatcher.
Today is the peak of the Lyrid meteor shower. Visible: 16-25 Apr, Peak: 22/23 Apr +MP:-04-22+, ZHR: 15-20, Radiant: Lyra. Bright fast meteors, some with trains. Associated with Comet Thatcher.
Today is the start of the Eta Aquarid meteor shower. Visible: 19 Apr-28 May, Peak: 6 May +MP:-05-06+, ZHR: 50, Radiant: Aquarius/Eta Aquarii. Low in sky. Associated with Comet Halley.
Today is the peak of the Eta Aquarid meteor shower. Visible: 19 Apr-28 May, Peak: 6 May +MP:-05-06+, ZHR: 50, Radiant: Aquarius/Eta Aquarii. Low in sky. Associated with Comet Halley.

Today is the start of the Delta Aquarid meteor shower. Visible: 12 Jul-23 Aug, Peak: 30 Jul +MP:-07-30+, ZHR: 25, Radiant: Aquarius/Delta Aquarii. Steady stream of meteors over several days but a low rate per hour.

Today is the peak of the Delta Aquarid meteor shower. Visible: 12 Jul-23 Aug, Peak: 30 Jul +MP:-07-30+, ZHR: 25, Radiant: Aquarius/Delta Aquarii. Steady stream of meteors over several days but a low rate per hour.

Today is the start of the Perseid meteor shower. Visible: 17 July-24 Aug, Peak: 13 Aug +MP:-08-13+, ZHR: of 100-150, Radiant: Perseus. Many bright fast meteors with trains. Associated with Comet Swift-Tuttle.

Today is the peak of the Perseid meteor shower. Visible: 17 July-24 Aug, Peak: 13 Aug +MP:-08-13+, ZHR: of 100-150, Radiant: Perseus. Many bright fast meteors with trains. Associated with Comet Swift-Tuttle.
Today is the start of the Draconid meteor shower. Visible: 6-10 Oct, Peak: 7 Oct +MP:-10-07+, ZHR: 5, Radiant: Draco. Associated with Comet 21/P Giacobini-Zimmer.
Today is the peak of the Draconid meteor shower. Visible: 6-10 Oct, Peak: 7 Oct +MP:-10-07+, ZHR: 5, Radiant: Draco. Associated with Comet 21/P Giacobini-Zimmer.
Today is the start of the Orionid meteor shower. Visible: 2 Oct-7 Nov, Peak: 21/22 Oct +MP:-10-22+, ZHR: 20, Radiant: Orion. Fast with fine trains. Associated with Comet Halley.
Today is the peak of the Orionid meteor shower. Visible: 2 Oct-7 Nov, Peak: 21/22 Oct +MP:-10-22+, ZHR: 20, Radiant: Orion. Fast with fine trains. Associated with Comet Halley.
Today is the start of the Leonid meteor shower. Visible: 6-30 Nov, Peak: 17/18 Nov +MP:-11-17+, ZHR: 10-15, Radiant: Leo. Fast bright meteors with fine trains. Associated with Comet Tempel-Tuttle.
Today is the peak of the Leonid meteor shower. Visible: 6-30 Nov, Peak: 17/18 Nov +MP:-11-17+, ZHR: 10-15, Radiant: Leo. Fast bright meteors with fine trains. Associated with Comet Tempel-Tuttle.
Today is the start of the Geminid meteor shower. Visible: 7-17 Dec, Peak: 13/14 Dec +MP:-12-13+, ZHR: 150, Radiant: Gemini. Plenty of bright meteors, few trains.
Today is the peak of the Geminid meteor shower. Visible: 7-17 Dec, Peak: 13/14 Dec +MP:-12-13+, ZHR: 150, Radiant: Gemini. Plenty of bright meteors, few trains.

The constellation of Sagittarius +SY:Sgr+ takes its name from the Latin for archer. The Sanskrit counterpart is Dhanus meaning bow. They are used as the 1st and 2nd months of the Darian calendar.

The constellation of Capricorn +SY:Cap+ takes its name from the Latin for goat's horn. The Sanskrit counterpart, Makara, refers to a sea-monster sometimes depicted as a crocodile. They are used as the 3rd and 4th months of the Darian calendar.

The constellation of Aquarius +SY:Aqr+ takes its name from the Latin for water-carrier. The Sanskrit counterpart is Kumbha, a type of pot used for water. They are used as the 5th and 6th months of the Darian calendar.

The constellation of Pisces +SY:Psc+ takes its name from the Latin for fish. The Sanskrit counterpart, Mina, has the same meaning. They are used as the names of the 7th and 8th months of the Darian calendar.

The constellation of Aries +SY:Ari+ takes its name from the Latin for ram. The Sanskrit counterpart is Mesha meaning sheep. They are used as the names of the 9th and 10th months of the Darian calendar.
The constellation of Taurus +SY:Tau+ takes its name from the Latin for bull. The Sanskrit counterpart, Rishabha, has the same meaning. They are used as the 11th and 12 months of the Darian calendar.
The constellation of Gemini +SY:Gem+ takes its name from the Latin for twins. The Sanskrit counterpart is Mithuna meaning paired. They are used as the 13th and 14th months of the Darian calendar.
The constellation of Cancer +SY:Cnc+ takes its name from the Latin for crab. The Sanskrit counterpart, Karka, has the same meaning. They are used as the 15th and 16th months of the Darian calendar.
The constellation of Leo +SY:Leo+ takes its name from the Latin for lion. The Sanskrit counterpart, Simha, has the same meaning. They are used as the 17th and 18th months of the Darian calendar.
The constellation of Virgo +SY:Vir+ takes its name from the Latin for maiden. The Sanskrit counterpart, Kanya, has the same meaning. They are used as the 19th and 20th months of the Darian calendar.
The constellation of Libra +SY:Lib+ takes its name from the Latin for scales. The Sanskrit counterpart, Tula, has the same meaning. They are used as the 21st and 22nd months of the Darian calendar.

The constellation of Scorpius +SY:Sco+ takes its name from the Latin for scorpion. The Sanskrit counterpart, Vrishika, has the same meaning. They are used as the 23rd and 24th months of the Darian calendar.
1M No.1 (USSR) aka Marsnik 1 launched. The first Soviet Mars mission, it failed to reach LEO.
1M No.2 (USSR) aka Marsnik 2 launched. A liquid oxygen spill froze the propellant and it was unable to achieve LEO.
2MV-4 No.1 (USSR) aka Sputnik 22, explodes in LEO. 22 pieces of debris tracked in decaying orbits over 4 months.
Mars 1 (USSR) aka Sputnik 23, launched. The first Soviet Mars mission to leave orbit. Contact was lost half way through its journey.
2MV-3 No.1 (USSR) aka Sputnik 24, fails to reach LEO.
Mariner 3 (NASA) the first American Mars mission fails during launch. Three weeks later, its twin is successfully launched for Mars.
Mariner 4 (NASA) probe was launched. It goes on to capture the first images of another planet ever returned from deep space.
Zond 2 (USSR) launched. Contact was lost before arrival.
Mariner 4 (NASA) flyby of Mars captures the first images of another planet taken from deep space.
Mariner 6 (NASA) probe was launched. A leak during pre-flight tests caused the 33m rocket to crumple but the payload was saved by daring technicians and launched on the rocket allocated for M7.
Mariner 7 (NASA) probe was launched, along with Mariner 6, it reached Mars 126 days later.
2M No.521 (USSR) fails to reach LEO.
2M No.522 (USSR) fails during launch. A fire in the first stage engine causes an engine shutdown 41 seconds after launch.
Mariner 6 (NASA) flyby of Mars captures images at the equator and acts as an advance scout for Mariner 7.
Mariner 7 (NASA) flyby surveyed the south polar ice cap and confirms trace amounts of water on Mars.
Mariner 8 (NASA) fails during launch. Three weeks later, its twin, M9, was successfully launched for Mars.
Kosmos 419 (USSR) fails to leave LEO. Its booster stage burn timer was set incorrectly.
Mars 2 (USSR) launched. It went on be the 2nd probe to orbit another planet, operating for 362 orbits over 18 hours.
Mars 3 (USSR) launched. It went on to be the 3rd spacecraft to orbit another planet, operating for 20 orbits.
Mariner 9 (NASA) launched. It arrives just ahead of the Soviet Mars 2 launched a week earlier.
Mariner 9 (NASA) becomes the 1st spacecraft to orbit another planet, two weeks ahead of Mars 2.
Mars 2 (USSR) orbiter reaches Mars, but its rover becomes the first to crash on the planet.
Mars 3 (USSR) becomes the 1st lander to make a soft landing on Mars. Contact lost after 110 seconds and the status of the rover is unknown.
Mariner 9 (NASA) deactivated 516 days after entering orbit. It was left in a decaying orbit and likely impacted Mars 50 years later in early 2022.
Mars 4 (USSR) orbiter launched. It would go on to reach Mars but fail to perform orbital insertion.
Mars 5 (USSR) orbiter launched. It would go on to reach Mars orbit and operate for 9 days.
Mars 6 (USSR) launched carrying a lander to collect atmospheric data. It would go on to fail during descent.
Mars 7 (USSR) lander launched, the 4th USSR mission in the 73' window. It would go on to separate prematurely and miss the planet.
Mars 4 (USSR) fails to perform orbital insertion burn but returns photos of Mars during flyby.
Mars 5 (USSR) enters Mars orbit. Contact lost after 9 days with 180 frames returned.
Mars 7 (USSR) reaches Mars but separated from coast stage prematurely and missed the planet.
Mars 6 (USSR) lander deployed. It returned data for 224 seconds during its descent before contact was lost.
Viking 1 (NASA) launched. It would be the longest running mission until Opportunity in 2010.
Viking 2 (NASA) launched to search for signs of life on Mars.
Viking 1 (NASA) becomes the 1st successful Mars lander. It operated for 2245 sols (2307 days).
Viking 2 (NASA) lander touches down on Mars at Utopia Planitia.
Viking 2 (NASA) orbiter shut down after 706 orbits and returning almost 16,000 images.
Viking 2 (NASA) lander runs down after operating for 1281 sols (1316 days).
Viking 1 (NASA) orbiter shut down after 1489 orbits.
Viking 1 (NASA) lander contact lost after a patch overwrites its antenna positioning software.
Phobos 1 (USSR) launched. It failed in transit due to a computer error on 2 Sep '88.
Phobos 2 (USSR) launched to explore the moons of Mars.
Phobos 2 (USSR) reaches Mars orbit. It returned 37 high resolution images of Phobos.
Phobos 2 (USSR) orbiter looses contact. The hopper and lander it carries are never deployed on Phobos.
Mars Observer (NASA) launched. Contact was lost on 24 Aug '93, 3 days before planned Mars orbit.
Mars Global Surveyor (NASA) launched. It would assist in future missions by making atmospheric observations.
Mars 96 (Roskosmos) fails to leave Earth orbit. It carried two landers and penetrators.
Pathfinder (NASA) launched carrying the Sojourner rover.
Pathfinder (NASA) lands. Sojourner, the first rover to operate on Mars, is deployed 2 sols later.
Mars Global Surveyor (NASA) achieves orbital insertion.
Sojourner rover (NASA) looses contact. It ran for 92 sols (95 days), three times longer than planned.
Nozomi (ISAS/Japan) launched. Its arrival was planned for Oct '99. Due to a fuel issue, it entered a heliocentric orbit and reached Mars 14 Dec '03.
Mars Climate Orbiter (NASA) launched, a smaller probe to avoid the high cost of previous losses.
Mars Polar Lander (NASA) launched. As well as a lander and penetrator, it carries a CD with a names of 1000 children from around the world.
Mars Climate Orbiter (NASA) miscalculates orbit insertion burn due to a unit conversion error, its fate is unknown.
Mars Polar Lander (NASA) starts atmospheric entry. Communications could not be reestablished and the craft is declared lost.
2001 Mars Odyssey (NASA) launched. As well as making atmospheric observations, it will be a relay for rovers.
2001 Mars Odyssey (NASA) arrives. It's the longest functioning probe and expected to continue running into 2025.
Mars Express (ESA) launched. It's the first Russian launched probe to successfully leave orbit since the Soviet Union fell.
Spirit (NASA) rover launched. It weighs 180kg and travels 0.18 km/h.
Opportunity (NASA) rover launched. It had to be delayed for 9 days due to high winds.
Nozomi (ISAS/Japan) reached Mars more than 4 years after its planned arrival. Fuel is depleted and it can not enter orbit. A flyby is performed instead.
Mars Express (ESA) arrives. The Beagle2 lander is lost when its solar panels fail to deploy but the orbiter could function till 2035.
Spirit (NASA) rover lands on Mars. Its mission was planned for 90 sols.
Opportunity (NASA) rover lands on the opposite side of Mars to its twin, spirit. It would operate for 5351 sols.
Mars Global Surveyor (NASA) becomes the first spacecraft to take a photo of another, the Mars Odyssey
Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (NASA) launched.
Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (NASA) enter orbit. It has been operating for 17 years and counting.
Mars Global Surveyor (NASA) suffers an error while attempting to reorient a solar panel and communication was lost.
Rosetta (ESA) performs a flyby of Mars on its way to comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko where it performed the first successful landing on a comet.
Phoenix (NASA) lander launched to study the polar region of Mars.
Phoenix (NASA) lander arrives on Mars, the 6th successful NASA landing.
Phoenix (NASA) lander sends its last message. Power from the solar panels had dropped over winter and contact could not be reestablished.
Dawn (NASA) probe performed a flyby of Mars on its way to study Vesta and Ceres in the asteroid belt.
Spirit (NASA) rover becomes embedded in sand on sol 1892 of its mission. It travelled 7.7km.
Spirit (NASA) rover looses contact on sol 2208 of its mission after spending 316 sols as a stationary platform.
The joint Fobos-Grunt (Roskosmos) / Yinghuo-1 (CNSA) launched. The engines failed in LEO and uncontrolled re-entry occurred on 15 Jan 2012.
Mars Science Laboratory (NASA) launched carrying the Curiosity rover.
Curiosity rover (NASA) lands. The mission was planned for 2 years, its now been operational for over 12 years and counting.
Mars Orbiter Mission (ISRO) launched from India. It was the first agency to successfully reach Mars on their maiden voyage.
MAVEN (NASA) orbiter launched. The name is an acronym for "Mars Atmosphere and Volatile Evolution".
MAVEN (NASA) achieves orbital insertion. It was planned to operate for 2 years and has achieved 11 years and counting.
Mars Orbiter Mission (ISRO) enters orbit. The mission was planned to operate for 6 months, it continued for over 6 years.
ExoMars 2016 launched from Baikonur. A joint mission carrying the ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter (ESA/Roscosmos) and Schiaparelli EDM lander.

ExoMars 2016 Schiaparelli EDM lander (ESA) attempts a soft landing on Mars. Opportunity rover was operating close by but was unable to track the decent. The crash was confirmed by orbiters over the following weeks.
InSight (NASA) launched, the lander was accompanied by the MarCO A/B probes.
Opportunity (NASA) rover looses contact on sol 5352 during a dust storm. It had travelled 45km and outlasted its original lifespan by 14 years.
InSight (NASA) lander is deployed. The MarCO A and B probes perform a flyby.
InSight (NASA) MarCO A probe makes its last contact after performing a flyby of Mars.
InSight (NASA) MarCO B probe makes its last contact after performing a flyby of Mars.
Emirates Mars Mission (MBRSC) orbiter, Hope, launched from the Tanegashima Space Center in Japan.
Tianwen-1 (CNSA) launched carrying an orbiter, a lander, a rover and 2 deployable cameras.
Mars 2020 (NASA) launched carrying the Perseverance rover and the Ingenuity copter.
Emirates Mars Mission (MBRSC) orbiter, Hope, enters orbit.
Tianwen-1 (CNSA) enters orbit.
Mars 2020 (NASA) the Perseverance rover lands on Mars.
Mars 2020 (NASA) the Ingenuity copter is deployed from Perseverance rover. It is the first aerodynamic flight on another planet.
Tianwen-1 (CNSA) lander touches down on Mars carrying the Zhurong rover.
Tianwen-1 (CNSA) lander deploys the Zhurong rover. It would operate for 347 sols (358 days).
Tianwen-1 (CNSA) orbiter releases its second deployable camera.
Tianwen-1 (CNSA) rover, Zhurong, enters hibernation over winter. It missed its expected wake date and orbiters confirm that it hasn't moved since.
Mars Orbiter Mission (ISRO) concluded. Contact had been lost in April and it's believed that the probe had run out of fuel. It operated for nearly 7 years.
InSight (NASA) lander makes its last contact. It operated for 1440 sols (4 years, 19 days).
Mars 2020 (NASA) the Ingenuity copter makes its last flight. It totalled 72 flights over 1035 sols (2 years, 9 months).
Europa Clipper (NASA) makes a flyby of Mars on its way to Jupiter's moon Europa where it's due to arrive April 2026.
Hera (ESA) makes a flyby of Mars and Deimos on its way to study asteroid Dimorphos four years after the DART impactor (NASA).
